# Brave Bunnies

**Brave Bunnies** (Ukrainian: Хоробрі зайці, romanized: *Khorobri zaitsi*) is a Ukrainian animated television series for preschool children aged 2 to 5. The series follows the adventures of two rabbit siblings, Bop and Boo, who travel with their family on the Bunny Bus and befriend animals from diverse environments. Created by Olga Cherepanova and produced by the Ukrainian company Glowberry in partnership with Spanish animation studio Ánima Kitchent, the series has been broadcast in more than 80 countries. The show emphasizes themes of diversity, acceptance, and healthy childhood development through its narrative of cross-cultural friendships and inclusive play. 

The first season premiered in December 2020 in Ukraine and subsequently achieved prominence as the first Ukrainian children's animated series to achieve significant international distribution. Production was interrupted by the Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, but resumed later that year following a partnership with Canadian entertainment company WildBrain, which became the majority stakeholder of the intellectual property in December 2022. The second season was released in 2023 and has continued the franchise's expansion across international markets. 

## Development and production

### Conception and early development

Brave Bunnies originated from a children's picture book created by Glowberry, a Ukrainian creative production company founded in 2009 that specialized in children's literature and illustration. Olga Cherepanova, the company's co-founder and creative producer, developed an initial concept featuring a family of rabbits embarking on a journey and meeting unusual animals. Cherepanova, who studied psychology, sought to create content that would encourage young children to respect and accept differences in others while supporting healthy childhood development. 

The project evolved from the picture book into a television series intended for children aged 2 to 5. Over the course of several years, Cherepanova and Glowberry worked to develop the concept into a fully animated series, recruiting international partners to ensure adequate funding and market access. Illustrator Anna Sarvira developed the visual style for the series, serving as art director, while Cherepanova served as creative producer. 

### International partnership

In 2019, production entered development as an international co-production involving Glowberry, Ánima Kitchent (the Spanish subsidiary of Mexican animation studio Ánima), and the Ukrainian State Film Agency and Ministry of Youth and Sports, which provided support. The production team brought together creative personnel from multiple countries, including British director Tim Fehrenbach and Canadian lead writer John Van Bruggen, both of whom had previous experience in children's animation. The production involved coordination among over 100 people working across different countries. 

The series was presented at industry events including MIPCOM in 2019, and by early 2020, the UK-based animation studio Aardman Animations had partnered with the production to serve as international distributor. Aardman secured additional sales at the 2020 Kidscreen Summit in Miami, positioning the series for international broadcast. At the subsequent MIPJunior market, the series became the second most-watched project, demonstrating strong industry interest. 

The first season consisted of 52 episodes, each seven minutes in length. 

### Production process and approach

The writing team for Brave Bunnies consulted with child psychologists throughout the development process to ensure that episodes would maintain the interest of young viewers, present stories supporting early socialization, and create characters representing diverse human personality types. Music celebrating the characters' achievements was composed in Ukraine. 

The production sought to present stories that would help introduce children to concepts of diversity and teach them to accept and communicate with people of different appearances and behaviors. Rather than simply portraying different characters, the show focused on depicting real-life scenarios demonstrating how to approach each individual uniquely, without pressure or expectation of conformity. 

### Impact of Russian invasion

Production of Brave Bunnies in Kyiv was suspended when the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022. Many members of the Glowberry team were forced to evacuate from Kyiv due to security concerns. Notably, production coordinator Natalia Yermak left her position at Glowberry to become a war correspondent and journalist for the New York Times, covering the conflict in Ukraine. 

Production remained halted for several months. However, by August 2022, production resumed following expressions of support from the production's international partners. In December 2022, Canadian children's entertainment company WildBrain became a majority stakeholder in Brave Bunnies, acquiring the rights to continue reliable production and distribution of the series. This partnership ensured that the second season could proceed without disruption. WildBrain's Vancouver animation studio joined Glowberry and Ánima Kitchent to produce the second season of 52 episodes. 

## Narrative and themes

The 2D animated series follows a family of rabbits consisting of two children—Bop and Boo—along with their parents (Ma and Pa) and four younger siblings known as the Bunny Babies. The family lives on the Bunny Bus, a vehicle they use to travel through the world they inhabit. Each episode begins with a cheerful song as the family travels to a new location. 

At each stop on their journey, brother Bop and sister Boo meet and befriend different animal characters, creating new games and activities with them. These interactions form the core narrative of each episode, allowing the show to introduce viewers to various animals and their distinct characteristics while modeling friendship-building and cooperative play. 

The series attempts to show preschool viewers the diversity of the world and to encourage acceptance of differences. Through the example of the Brave Bunnies characters, who approach each new friend with openness and curiosity, the show demonstrates how to communicate with and befriend people with different appearances and behaviors. Beginning in the second season, some episodes feature the bunny family revisiting friends at their homes, meeting their families, and learning about different lifestyles. 

## Release and broadcast

### Initial premiere and distribution

The series premiered on December 5, 2020, on PLUSPLUS, a Ukrainian television channel. Following the Ukrainian premiere, the series entered international broadcast, launching on major networks including Nick Jr. (United Kingdom), Super RTL (Germany), ABC (Australia), Yle (Finland), and HOP! (Israel). By 2022, the first season had been broadcast in more than 80 countries. 

Aardman Animations distributed the first season internationally, leveraging its established relationships with broadcasters and distribution partners worldwide. The series appeared on prominent children's programming blocks, including Milkshake! on Channel 5 in the United Kingdom (beginning February 6, 2021) and ABC Kids in Australia. In Canada, the series was broadcast on WildBrain's Family Jr. channel, and in the United States, episodes became available on the WildBrain+ SVOD platform on Comcast. 

### Second season and expanded distribution

The second season was released in Canada in June 2023, followed by other territories later that year. Following WildBrain's acquisition of majority control, the company expanded the series' international distribution network. As of 2023, distribution deals were in place with platforms across Latin America, Canada, the United Kingdom, Europe, the Nordic countries, the Middle East, Asia, and Australia. Notable distribution partnerships included TeleTOON+ (Poland), Rai Yoyo (Italy), and renewed partnerships with existing broadcasters including Milkshake! in the United Kingdom. 

In Southeast Asia and across the Asia-Pacific region, the series was made available through Warner Media's Cartoon Network and streaming platform HBO GO. The series also became available on YouTube, including through the Sunflower TV channel, which launched in July 2022 to provide ad-free Ukrainian-language children's content for Ukrainian refugees across Europe and the United Kingdom. 

## Voice cast

The original Ukrainian voice cast included prominent performers. Actress Olena Kravets provided the voice for Bunny Ma, while musician and songwriter Potap voiced Bunny Pa. The casting of such high-profile Ukrainian performers was noted as significant, as it marked the first time a Ukrainian children's animated series had attracted voice talent of this caliber, according to reports by 1+1 Media. 

The English-language dub featured different voice actors: Wilbur Conabeare as Bop, Margot Powell as Boo, Harriet Kershaw as Bunny Ma, Jensen Adeyanju as Bunny Pa, and Chetna Pandya as Narrator. 

## Reception

Brave Bunnies achieved strong viewership ratings in multiple international markets. The series was among the top-rated children's programs in Ukraine, the United Kingdom, Israel, and Australia. In the United Kingdom, the series ranked as the number one program in its broadcast slots at its premiere on the Milkshake! platform and subsequently reached an audience of 4.4 million viewers. 

In 2020, the British research agency Childwise conducted a focus group study of children aged 3 to 5 who watched the series. The study found that 79 percent of children reported feeling happier after watching episodes, and 90 percent indicated they liked the characters. The publication The New Voice of Ukraine praised the series for its message of diversity and acceptance. 

The series received recognition at international animation festivals and industry events. It became a finalist at Animation Production Day (Germany), Cartoon Forum (France), Cartoon 360 (Spain), and the International Animated Film Festival MIFA (France). The series also received consideration at the Financing Forum for Kids Content (Sweden) and the Ottawa International Animation Festival (Canada). 

## Merchandise and publishing

Merchandise based on the series was developed through partnerships with major consumer products companies. In April 2022, Spin Master, a global toy manufacturer, launched a line of Brave Bunnies plush toys and other merchandise in Germany and Italy. 

Publishing deals expanded the brand into books. De Agostini's Planeta Libre imprint published books in Italy, Five Mile Publishing released titles in Australia, and Ladybird (an imprint of Penguin Random House) launched a series of preschool storybooks in the United Kingdom beginning in early 2022. WildBrain CPLG, the consumer products division of WildBrain, manages global licensing and merchandising for the brand (excluding Ukraine and Italy).

_**Brave Bunnies**_ ([Ukrainian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_language "Ukrainian language"): Хоробрі зайці, [romanized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanization_of_Ukrainian "Romanization of Ukrainian"): _Khorobri zaitsi_) is a [Ukrainian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_in_Ukraine "Television in Ukraine") [children's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children%27s_television_series "Children's television series") [animated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animated_series "Animated series") television series for [preschool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preschool "Preschool") children aged 2 to 5. In the series, two rabbit children show their courage when they meet and befriend other animals. Creator Olga Cherepanova sought to encourage respect for diversity and to promote healthy childhood development.

The series has been broadcast in more than 80 countries. The first season was produced by Glowberry and [Ánima Kitchent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81nima_/(company/) "Ánima (company)") in partnership with distributor [Aardman Animations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aardman_Animations "Aardman Animations"), and premiered in December 2020. Production of the second season was interrupted by the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"), and resumed in December 2022 after [WildBrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WildBrain "WildBrain") acquired a majority ownership of the property. A second season was distributed by WildBrain in 2023.

The 2D animated series follows the adventures of a family of rabbits:[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) Boo and Bop, Ma and Pa, and four Bunny Babies.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-SartoBunnies-2) Every episode starts with a cheerful song as the family ride on their bunny bus, which stops at a new location. Brother Bop and sister Boo then explore and make friends with a different animal, creating a new game to play with them. The series attempts to show its preschool viewers the diversity of the world and to accept the differences of others.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) Starting in the second season, some episodes have the bunny family revisit friends at their homes, meeting their families and learning more about their different lifestyles.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3)

The series introduces children to the concept of diversity and, through the example of the Brave Bunnies, shows how to accept and communicate with people possessing different appearances and behaviours.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguide-4)[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) To promote healthy childhood development, characters Bop and Boo acknowledge the uniqueness of each new friend.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-WildbrainPrimary3-5)

The Ukrainian voice cast includes actress [Olena Kravets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olena_Kravets "Olena Kravets") and singer-songwriter [Potap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potap "Potap"), which [1+1 Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1%2B1_Media "1+1 Media") stated was the first time a Ukrainian children's animated series attracted such high-profile performers.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-1+1Cast-6)

*   Narrator – Chetna Pandya (English dub)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)
*   Bop – Wilbur Conabeare (English dub)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)
*   Boo – Margot Powell (English dub)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)
*   Bunny Ma – [Olena Kravets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olena_Kravets "Olena Kravets") (Ukrainian),[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-1+1Cast-6) Harriet Kershaw (English dub)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)
*   Bunny Pa – [Potap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potap "Potap") (Ukrainian),[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-1+1Cast-6) Jensen Adeyanju (English dub)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)

Development and production
--------------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brave_Bunnies&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Development and production")\]

Publishing house Glowberry was founded in 2009 and worked in children's literature and illustration,[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-PrimaryGlowberry-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-FilmUA-9) seeking to create modern fairy tales. Their best-selling work was a picture book about a family of rabbits on a journey, meeting unusual animals as they travelled further from their home. Several years were spent developing this into a television series[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) for children aged 2 to 5.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3) Glowberry co-founder and series creator Olga Cherepanova[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12) noted that while rabbits are often considered to be timid animals, their bravery in the series comes from discovering new challenges every day.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) She said that she created the series "to help children ... communicate with different friends without any fears or stereotypes, respecting the diversity of our world."[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-SartoBunnies-2)

Illustrator Anna Sarvira[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-13) developed the style for the series, serving as art director while Cherepanova was the creative producer.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12) Following this early creative work, the production became an international project to ensure funding, market access, and expertise. Over a hundred people in different countries were involved, coordinating together on the same schedule.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) This included British director Tim Fehrenbach and Canadian lead writer John Van Bruggen, both of whom had experience in children's animation.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12) Cherepanova was educated in psychology, and the writing team consulted with [child psychologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_psychology "Developmental psychology") throughout the process. They sought to maintain the interest of young children, present stories that would aid [early socialisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_socialization "Primary socialization"), and create characters representing the many different human [personality types](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personality_type "Personality type").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) The music which celebrates the characters' achievements in each episode was composed in Ukraine.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14)

In 2019, the series was in development with Glowberry and Ánima Kitchent (the Spanish subsidiary of Mexico-based animation studio [Ánima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81nima_/(company/) "Ánima (company)")).[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-PulidoAnima-15) The production also received support from the [Ukrainian State Film Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_State_Film_Agency "Ukrainian State Film Agency") and the [Ministry of Youth and Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Youth_and_Sports_/(Ukraine/) "Ministry of Youth and Sports (Ukraine)").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-UkrinformItaly-16) Glowberry pitched the series to studios and distributors at [MIPCOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIPCOM "MIPCOM") in 2019. By early 2020, UK studio [Aardman Animations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aardman_Animations "Aardman Animations") had partnered as the international distributor and secured additional international sales at the 2020 [Kidscreen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidscreen "Kidscreen") Summit in Miami.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) The first season consisted of 52 seven-minute episodes.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1)

When the full-scale [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine") began in February 2022, the production of _Brave Bunnies_ in Kyiv was suspended.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YermakReporter-17) Many of the Glowberry team were forced to flee Kyiv,[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11) and production coordinator Natalia Yermak became a war correspondent for the _[New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Times "New York Times")_.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YermakReporter-17) Production resumed in August[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) and by December 2022, Canadian children's entertainment company [WildBrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WildBrain "WildBrain") became a majority stakeholder in _Brave Bunnies_, to continue the reliable production and distribution of the series.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11) WildBrain took over global distribution of the series, merchandising and licensing, and the company's Vancouver animation studio joined Glowberry and Ánima Kitchent[\[b\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-20) to produce the second season of 52 episodes.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TownsendWildbrain-21)

The series premiered on 5 December 2020 on [PLUSPLUS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PLUSPLUS "PLUSPLUS") in Ukraine, followed by [Nick Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Jr. "Nick Jr.") (UK), [Super RTL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_RTL "Super RTL") (Germany), [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Television_/(Australian_TV_network/) "ABC Television (Australian TV network)") (Australia), [Yle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yle "Yle") (Finland), and [HOP!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hop!_Channel "Hop! Channel") (Israel).[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12) The first season was distributed by Aardman Animations,[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) and by 2022 had been broadcast in over 80 countries.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3)

_Brave Bunnies_ streamed on the [Sunflower TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower_TV "Sunflower TV") YouTube channel, which launched in July 2022 and allowed [Ukrainian refugees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_refugee_crisis "Ukrainian refugee crisis") across Europe and the UK to watch ad-free children's programming in the Ukrainian language.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MchughSunflower-22)[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-EvansSunflower-23) Content was approved by a panel of media professionals, child psychologists and Ukrainian mothers. The creators of _Brave Bunnies_ along with partner companies waived their rights to enable the project.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MchughSunflower-22)[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-EvansSunflower-23)

It is broadcast on WildBrain's [Family Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_Jr. "Family Jr.") channel in Canada[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-BrzoznowskiWildbrain-24)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-BabieraWildbrain-25) and on the Comcast WildBrain+ [SVOD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_on_demand#Subscription_models "Video on demand") channel in the United States.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-SenalWildbrain-18) The second season was released in Canada in June 2023[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TownsendWildbrain-21) followed by other territories later that year.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TodoWildbrain-26)

_Brave Bunnies_ was among the top-rated children's programs in Ukraine, the UK, Israel and Australia.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) _[The New Voice of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Voice_of_Ukraine "The New Voice of Ukraine")_ applauded its message of diversity and acceptance.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14) A 2020 focus group by British research agency Childwise found that 79% of children aged 3 to 5 felt happier after watching the series, and 90% liked the characters.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14)

Books and merchandising
-----------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brave_Bunnies&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Books and merchandising")\]

Glowberry first distributed its books through the company's tablet app.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-FilmUA-9) Following the launch of the TV series, various publishers were licensed to print physical books for _Brave Bunnies_, beginning with Italian-language editions by [Planeta Libre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Agostini "De Agostini")[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-UkrinformItaly-16)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-WildbrainPrimary3-5) in 2021.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14) English-language editions were published by [Penguin Random House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_Random_House "Penguin Random House") imprint Ladybird Books. These children's books include picture books ([board books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_book "Board book")), [colouring books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coloring_book "Coloring book"), [activity books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activity_book "Activity book"), and sticker books.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10)

Canadian multinational toy company [Spin Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_Master "Spin Master") created a line of toys for the franchise.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11) The toy line includes figures, playsets, games, and plushies.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Toybook-27)

12 October 2023 // [News](https://www.skwigly.co.uk/articles/news/ "News")

![Image 1](https://www.skwigly.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Ukraines-Glowberry-Series-Mom-Hurries-Home.jpeg)

Credit: Glowberry

This year, Ukraine will bring to MIPCOM a new animated project – _Mom Hurries Home_ by [Glowberry production studio](https://glowberry.com/en), famous for the _Brave Bunnies_ animated series.

Every day, Mom turns her daily trips home from work into magical adventure stories, inspired by her son Alex’s fantasy games. Together, they are transforming their humdrum city into a magical place. The main idea of the project – kids and parents could play the same game, making everyday extraordinary by their imagination.

_Mom Hurries Home_ was first presented at MIP Junior in 2016. After that, the creative concept of the series became the finalist at major European animation festivals, and beyond: International Animated Film Festival MIFA (France), Cartoon Forum (France), Animation Production Day (Germany), Cartoon 360 (Spain), Financing Forum for Kids Content (Sweden), Ottawa International Animation Festival (Canada) in 2016-2019. Along with _Mavka__:_ _The Forest Song_, from Animagrad Studio ([FILM.UA](http://film.ua/) Group), it was the first Ukrainian animated project to get through the competitions and represent Ukraine at these important industry platforms.

Besides, _Mom Hurries Home_ is a successful Ukrainian brand, developed from a series of books by Sveta Dorosheva (Ukraine/Israel) that quickly became popular among children and parents alike. The series was also published in China and South Korea, where it gained noticeable success as well. The interactive version of the books for Android and iOS have had more than 80,000 downloads in over 10 European countries. Building on this success, Glowberry production together with [FILM.UA](http://film.ua/) Group began the development of the preschool TV series.

By 2019, the project was appreciated by broadcasters in Europe and Asia, and global distributors and co-partners expressed interest. Now, _Mom Hurries Home_ is a 52-episodes × 7 min project in development, for kids aged 4-7. The author of the TV series concept is Olga Cherepanova, showrunner, content creator, and creative producer at Glowberry. This is her second big animated project after the _Brave Bunnies_ animated series, which achieved thrilling international success: its first season was aired in over 80 countries.

_Brave Bunnies_ is an animated TV series that follows the adventures of the Brave Bunnies Family, on their exciting Big Journey to explore the wider world, where they discover diverse new friends. The first season (52×7) was created by Glowberry in co-partnership with the Ánima Studio (Spain), and co-producer De Agostini (Italy), while multi-award-winning animation studio Aardman Animations (United Kingdom) was engaged in the global promotion. Penguin Random House became the official global book partner, while the leading global children’s entertainment company, Spin Master, launched a toy collection with the heroes of the series in 2021 across multiple European territories.

The first launch of _Brave Bunnies_ Season 1 took place at the end of 2021 on the Ukrainian TV channel Plus-Plus. Since then, it has aired in more than 80 countries around the world with global broadcast partners including Milkshake/Channel5, Nick Jr, Rai YoYo, ABC Kids, HBO Max, Family Jr., Clan, SuperRTL, NRK, SVT, DeA Junior, YLE, RTP, Ceska TV, HOP, Daeyko TV, and other.

The full-scale attack of Russia on Ukraine in early 2022 threatened to dramatically change the plans for the second season of _Brave Bunnies_. But international partners rallied to support Glowberry, and at the end of 2022, the leading Canadian kids’ entertainment company WildBrain partnered with Glowberry to bring the beloved _Brave Bunnies_ brand into its portfolio of kids’ and family franchises, taking a majority stake in the IP. The partnership gave Cherepanova a leading role in _Brave Bunnies_ animation for Season 2, as creator and creative producer, while keeping all the Ukrainian Glowberry team. Production of the second season of _Brave Bunnies_ is under way in partnership with Spanish animation studio Ánima and Italian co-producer De Agostini. With season one, _Brave Bunnies_ achieved prominent international success, and its creators are planning an exciting and entertaining follow up with season two.

And now, with _Mom Hurries Home_, Glowberry looks for broadcasters in Europe and Asia, and interest from global distributors and co-partners for it newest show.

> Mom Hurries Home is an exciting concept that allows us to infuse the daily lives of children and their parents with magic and wonder through the power of imagination. Drawing from our unique and successful experience working on two seasons of the hit preschool show Brave Bunnies, we have enhanced the initial creative concept for Mom Hurries Home, making the show even more aligned with the expectations of today’s parents and children, and we’ve also taken into account the feedback and preferences of international broadcasters.
> 
> **Olga Cherepanova**

Despite the war, Ukrainian production companies continue developing new large-scale projects, often in co-production with partners from all around the world. The latest achievements of _Brave Bunnies_ and _Mavka_ prove that the creative stories by Ukrainian authors are interesting, inspiring, and uplifting for the worldwide audience, bringing fresh new ideas and views.

Ukraine’s Glowberry brings toon project Mom Hurries Home back to Mipcom
=======================================================================

![Image 4](https://cdn.c21media.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/mom-hurries-home.jpg)

Mom Hurries Home was first pitched at MipJunior in 2016

Ukrainian animation studio Glowberry is heading to Mipcom with its latest animated series, Mom Hurries Home – seven years after the war-disrupted project was first presented to MipJunior delegates.

The series was first pitched at MipJunior in 2016 and made it to the finals of various competitions at animation festivals including MIFA (France), Cartoon Forum (France), Animation Production Day (Germany) and Cartoon 360 (Spain).

Now Glowberry, the Film.UA Group studio behind Brave Bunnies, is unveiling the 52×7’ series in Cannes next week.

A show for four- to seven-year-olds, Mom Hurries Home was developed from a series of books by Sveta Dorosheva and adapted into a series by Olga Cherepanova, showrunner, content creator and creative producer at Glowberry.

An interactive version of the Mom Hurries Home book series has already become something of a hit, with some 80,000 downloads in 10 European markets. The show centres on a mum who turns her daily trips home from work into magical adventure stories, inspired by her son’s fantasy games.

“Mom Hurries Home is an exciting concept that allows us to infuse the daily lives of children and their parents with magic and wonder through the power of imagination,” said Cherepanova, whose credits include Brave Bunnies.

The first season of Brave Bunnies debuted on Ukrainian channel Plus-Plus in 2021 and aired in more than 80 countries around the world. Canada’s Wildbrain later came onboard and acquired a majority stake in the IP. Production on a second season is underway, in partnership with Spanish animation studio Ánima and Italian coproducer De Agostini.

Glowberry said the success of Brave Bunnies and another Ukrainian animation, Mavka: The Forest Song, from fellow Film.UA subsidiary Animagrad Studio, prove that despite the Russian invasion of the country last year, “the creative stories by Ukrainian authors are interesting, inspiring and uplifting for the worldwide audience, bringing fresh new ideas and views.”

14.title: VGhlIEFzdG9uaXNoaW5nIEJyYXZlcnkgb2YgdGhlIFRlYW0gQmVoaW5kIFVrcmFpbmXigJlzIEJyYXZlIEJ1bm5pZXM=
14.content:
**Olga Cherepanova and her team at Glowberry, creators of the only global Ukrainian children’s property, Brave Bunnies, are astonishing in their personal strength, commitment and gratitude to partners. With a name that could not be more apt, preschool series BRAVE BUNNIES was on an upward trajectory before the unimaginable happened in their hometown of Kyiv, Ukraine, with global partners, agents, broadcasters and more jumping at the chance to work with the bunnies, whose ethos is friendship and kindness.**

As this article is being written, some of the team may have fled horror and war and become refugees while the rest of the team are stuck in Ukraine or volunteering to support refugees and national defence, but they remain as determined as ever to continue the very brave mission of their BRAVE BUNNIES. At a time when the world is watching with utter despair as events in Ukraine unfold, the BRAVE BUNNIES symbolise the resilience and optimism and spirit of the Ukrainian people.

**Olga outlines here, in a heartfelt piece, what the recent events mean for her, her team of creators, and the extremely successful Ukrainian export, BRAVE BUNNIES.**

“I really want to write today, amidst all that is happening, that I am incredibly proud of Ukraine.  Here live beautiful and talented people! Three years ago, here in Kyiv, we came up with the idea for our project BRAVE BUNNIES, which is now successfully broadcast in more than 63 countries.  My initial intention was to tell everyone how crucial it is to respect the diversity of this world. At the time, this topic sounded to me like it was the most important for the younger generation. They are about to live in a time when human migration is coming to the fore and will probably become increasingly important due to global climate change. And now, in the terrible situation the whole world has had to face, especially my beloved Ukraine, this message has become even more important.”

![Image 1](https://www.totallicensing.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Screenshot-2022-03-11-at-10.46.29.png)

“The big mission of BRAVE BUNNIES is to show kids that it is important to respect the difference of others and their boundaries.  We follow our main characters as they meet new friends who are very different from each other – just like all of us! Each episode shows real-life examples of how to find an approach to each person without pressure or changing their uniqueness.  This big idea quickly attracted many partners from different countries and wonderful professionals from all over the world – Spain, UK, Italy, USA, Canada, Mexico and many more – to our project. Working on the show has been a great lesson in tolerance, support, and understanding of different points of view and cultures. Together we are making a product that is enjoyed by children all over the world.”

“Every one of our partners wrote us a warm letter of support today and suggested real help, and that is so precious, friends. Thank you!  But my post today is first of all about how proud I am of our Brave Bunnies Ukrainian Team. This picture is two years old, and on it, unfortunately, it doesn’t present all the talented and beautiful people working on the project in Ukraine – coming up with ideas, drawing illustrations, writing music, and organizing the team of 100 people on three continents and in many countries. They all have long become more than just colleagues, they are close friends and amazing people.  I don’t have a more recent picture, but I’m waiting for better times to make it for sure!”

“For now, our BRAVE BUNNIES team is apart, focusing on protecting their homes and their country.  “Our lives have been completely overhauled in a single day, but they are still our ‘previous’ lives: in the midst of sirens and bombing and unfunctional roads, we have to try and get food, arrange for some drinkable water. We save our lives and the lives of our loved ones. We pack everything into one small backpack and leave everything we have built and loved. We leave and lose our loved ones. We experience feelings that two weeks ago we never thought we would experience in our prosperous life, which we have been building so hard and for so long…  And most importantly, now each of us already knows that the most precious thing in this world – human life and safety – can be violated in an instant.”

“We hope to be together again soon to continue with our show and take more recent photos.  Also, I really hope that my idea that you can always find a way to create something beautiful together without conflict will find even more resonance in the world today, and the new generation will know exactly how to accomplish it.  We strongly hope that the horror that is happening now will end as soon as possible, and we will be able to return to normal life. We thank everyone who helped us in these first hard days of the war, opened their hearts, the doors of their homes, and shared the essentials.  We are very grateful to all our partners who help the project move forward. It gives us hope that together we can bring back a prosperous time for all.”

![Image 2](https://www.totallicensing.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Screenshot-2022-03-11-at-10.46.47.png)

After the first presentation of BRAVE BUNNIES at the Cartoon Forum Festival in Toulouse in 2019, it was then the most-viewed preschool show at MIPCOM 2020. Since then, Glowberry has worked with its global master agents Big Picture Licensing and Panderia to create the brand strategy and sign-up strategic best in-class partners for wave #1. As Olga herself says, “BRAVE BUNNIES had a quick and very brave start!” Partnerships soon followed with Aardman as the global content distribution partner, Spin Master as global master toy licensee, DeAgostini as a 360 partner for Italy, Penguin Random House as multi-territory publisher and PMI for global Collectables and BTS.  Agents were actively signing up the first local licensees for wave #2 rollout including Roy Lowe, Five Mile Press and Caprice when the unprecedented crisis hit. Licensing agents are signed up around the world for wave #1 launch, including WildBrain CPLG (CEE/Nordic/Benelux/Greece/Turkey), El Ocho (Iberia), CLM (Africa), Mediogen (Israel), and KidsMe/DeAgostini (Italy).  Centa IP was recently appointed as the exclusive licensing agent for Australia and New Zealand.

The global interest in the BRAVE BUNNIES certainly lies in the beautiful and unique animation, the storytelling, and the very relevant messages in each episode that resonate with families wanting to bring safe and positive content to their children, alongside themes of friendship, diversity and inclusivity.  Season 1 launched Jan. 2021 with 52 episodes and broadcast partners include Milkshake/Channel5, Nick Jr, Rai YoYo, ABC Kids, HBO Max, Clan, SuperRTL, NRK, SVT, DeA Junior, YLE, RTP, Ceska TV, HOP and Daeyko TV. The production of season 2, as Olga puts it “was well underway when the iceberg hit us.”

Glowberry and all parties remain extremely committed to the property and are enormously proud to bring the first Ukrainian kids brand to a global audience. BRAVE BUNNIES remains a trusted brand with pro-social values and an emphasis on fun.

Nothing will keep Olga, the BRAVE BUNNIES and the roaster of supportive partners down. Spin Master has launches planned in 2022 across multiple European territories; Planeta Libri continues to rollout new books in Italy and Penguin Random House are planning an imminent launch of books in the UK for Easter as well as additional markets.

“We just want peace for our country,” Olga says. “To be able to continue our lives and business with our international partners and continue to bring our BRAVE BUNNIES to new audiences worldwide across broadcast platforms and consumer products.  From the Glowberry team, we would like to thank all of our broadcast and consumer products partners for your continued support during this crisis.”

**For more information:**

[**www.bravebunnies.com**](http://www.bravebunnies.com/)

18.content:
**Glowberry and WarnerMedia bring BRAVE BUNNIES series to APAC**

_BRAVE BUNNIES will launch soon on Cartoonito – Cartoon Network’s preschool block – and streaming on HBO GO in Southeast Asia  
_**Ukraine, Kyiv – April, 2022**

**Glowberry**, the Ukrainian creator of a widely popular kids’ series BRAVE BUNNIES, has announced a licensing agreement with **WarnerMedia,** the leading media and entertainment company, to broadcast the series in 20 territories across Southeast Asia, as well as Australia and New Zealand. The deal was secured for Glowberry by its exclusive content distribution partner, **Aardman**, who have been leading the charge for BRAVE BUNNIES with tier #1 broadcasters around the world.

The series will premiere on the **Cartoonito** pre-school programming block available daily on **Cartoon Network**, which launched on March 28 in Southeast Asia, and will debut in Australia and New Zealand in July. All Cartoonito shows follow a curriculum designed by early childhood education expert Dr Laura Brown to support the four pillars of Humancentric Learning: Creativity, Caring, Curiosity and Courage. The brand aims to inspire kids to use their imagination, to learn from their mistakes and to treat others with empathy and respect.

The series will also be available to stream in Southeast Asia, Taiwan and Hong Kong on **HBO GO**.This latest deal strengthens the relationship with **WarnerMedia** as BRAVE BUNNIES was also acquired by **HBO Max** for LATAM. The series will premiere mid-2022.

**Olga Cherepanova, author and creative producer of BRAVE BUNNIES**, comments:

_We are delighted that a show we have been working on so passionately has been expanding so fast. I’m happy that alongside WarnerMedia we will reach a new audience in APAC. We wish viewers exciting time along with the BRAVE BUNNIES! Our partner Aardman continues to do a great job signing up the best broadcast partners for our BRAVE BUNNIES._

BRAVE BUNNIES is a brand new and unique entertainment and educational series for preschool kids. It tells the story of the curious and courageous brother and sister – Bop and Boo – who, together with their Brave Bunnies family, travel exploring the world around them and making new friends. Some of these are very much unlike the Bunnies, yet they always get a bunny-brilliant idea on how to make friends with them, invent a new game, and have a lot of fun together.

**Robin Gladman, Head of Acquisitions at Aardman**, comments:

_It’s a great pleasure to be working with our friends at Glowberry, to help bring Brave Bunnies to the world. The team from Ukraine are constantly in our thoughts in their current plight. Friendship and diversity sit at the core of this fabulous show, these messages are more important now than ever, and we are thrilled Warner have decided to come on board across so many territories._

[­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­BRAVE BUNNIES](https://bravebunnies.com/) is a brand-new unique entertainment and educational series for preschool kids. It tells the story of the curious and courageous brother and sister – Bop and Boo, who, together with their Brave Bunnies family, travel exploring the world around them and making new friends. Some of these are very much unlike the Bunnies, yet they always get a BunnyBriliant idea on how to make friends with them, invent a new game, and have a lot of fun together. The project is created in co-production with a Spanish animation studio – Ánima. The team includes the Director – Tim Fehrenbach (Great Britain), and the Head Writer for the series – John van Bruggen (Canada), who has extensive experience in creating kids’ animated content. The visual style of the series is created by a famous Ukrainian illustrator Anna Sarvira (Ukraine). The project is created with the support of FILM.UA Group, the State Film Agency, and the Ministry of Youth and Sports of Ukraine.

[Glowberry](https://glowberry.com/en) is a Ukrainian creative production that develops high-quality content 360° for Kids and families worldwide, founded in 2009 as a publishing house. Glowberry, now a part of FILM.UA Group, grew into a production company with a big international team. Today, one of the key projects for our team is the BRAVE BUNNIES animated series. The projects of our professional team are highly acclaimed by international experts and became shortlist finalists of global animation festivals like Cartoon Forum, Animation Production Day, Cartoon 360, Annecy International Animated Film Festival (MIFA), Ottawa International Animation Festival, The Financing Forum for Kids Content.

**About WarnerMedia**

WarnerMedia is a leading media and entertainment company that creates and distributes premium and popular content from a diverse array of talented storytellers and journalists to global audiences through its consumer brands, including: HBO, HBO Max, Warner Bros., TNT, TBS, truTV, CNN, DC, New Line, Cartoon Network, Adult Swim, Turner Classic Movies and others. WarnerMedia is part of AT&T Inc. (NYSE:T).

**About Aardman**

[Aardman](http://www.aardman.com/), based in Bristol (UK) and co-founded in 1976 by Peter Lord and David Sproxton, is an independent and multi-Academy Award® and BAFTA® award winning studio. It produces feature films, series, advertising, games and interactive entertainment – current animated productions include; 2021 holiday specials Robin Robin and Shaun the Sheep: The Flight Before Christmas, CGI series Lloyd of the Flies, a new stop motion series for pre-schoolers The Very Small Creatures, feature length sequel Chicken Run: Dawn of the Nugget and a brand new Wallace & Gromit film for 2024.

Its productions are global in appeal, novel, entertaining, brilliantly characterised and full of charm reflecting the unique talent, energy and personal commitment of the Aardman team. The studio’s work – which includes the creation of much-loved characters including [Wallace & Gromit](https://www.wallaceandgromit.com/), [Shaun the Sheep](https://www.shaunthesheep.com/), [Timmy Time](https://www.timmytime.tv/) and [Morph](https://amazingmorph.com/) – is often imitated, and yet the company continues to lead the field producing a rare brand of visually stunning content for cinema, broadcasters, digital platforms and live experiences around the world. Recent celebrated projects include the ‘visually astonishing’ (Guardian), BAFTA® nominated console game, [11-11: Memories Retold](https://www.aardman.com/film-tv-games/11-11-memories-retold/), the four-times Gold Cannes Lions-winning [StorySign](https://www.aardman.com/interactive/storysign/) app, AR experience Wallace & Gromit: The Big Fix up – and innovative attractions for both the domestic and international market, including a [4D theatre attraction](https://www.aardman.com/short-form-commercials/the-bear-and-the-squirrel/) at Efteling in the Netherlands.

The studio runs the [Aardman Academy](https://academy.aardman.com/), which has a commitment to nurturing talent by delivering excellence in film and animation training and mentoring. The Aardman Academy offers a variety of courses from intensive one-day workshops teaching production skills and storyboarding, to comprehensive twelve-week courses for professionals in craft based subjects from model making to animation.

In November 2018 it became an Employee Owned Organisation, to ensure Aardman remains independent and to secure the creative legacy and culture of the company for many decades to come. www.aardman.com

17.content:
Published 29th October 2020

Brave Bunnies – a 52 x 7 minute 2D pre-school series created by Olga Cherepanova, currently in production with family entertainment company Anima and distributed globally by Aardman, has received positive reviews from the most influential international experts and became one of the projects receiving most viewed programmes in the [MIPJunior](https://www.mipjunior.com/en-gb.html) screenings library.

The animated series, which is yet to see its international premiere on the world’s TV channels, received a very positive response when presented at entertainment content market MIPCOM earlier this month, and was charted as the second most watched project during the first week of the market.

**Alison Taylor, Director of Distribution and Business Development at Aardman says**: “We were delighted to see Brave Bunnies feature in the top screening figures at MIPJunior, and to hear first-hand from buyers about what they love about the series during our meetings at Mipcom Online+. From the discussions had at the market, we’re confident that we will soon be in a position to announce further partnerships on the brand, in addition to the excellent broadcaster partners already announced.”

**Olga Cherepanova, Author of the original idea of the series and Creative Producer at Glowberry added**: “We are incredibly happy that Brave Bunnies have managed to attract so much attention from the MIPJunior participants, since their expertise is of great importance to us and proves that we are moving in the right direction and are indeed creating the content of international level. As for now, we have quite an ambitious plan, which is gradually being implemented – to captivate the hearts of an audience of at least fifty, and better even a hundred countries of the world.“

**Ángel Molinero, CEO (Spain) at Ánima concluded**: “Brave Bunnies is such a great show, the amazing performance it had during MipJunior proves it. We are honoured to be part of such a unique show and eager to introduce the Bunny family to kids all around the world.”

Deals for the series have been secured with Nick Jr (UK), Super RTL (Germany), ABC (Australia), YLE (Finland), HOP! (Israel), PlusPlus (Ukraine), Daekyo (South Korea) and Milkshake! (UK).

Brave Bunnies follows a family of courageous and curious Bunnies as they seek adventure and exploration, travelling on the Bunny Bus. Every episode in the series, directed by Tim Fehrenbach starts with a Bunny Bus-ride. On each stop, brother and sister Bunnies, Bop and Boo discover different animals, creating new games to help build new friendships. The series shows children the diversity of the world, encouraging viewers to accept differences, no matter how big or small.

[Brave Bunnies](https://bravebunnies.com/) is due to launch in winter 2020.

**New international partnerships include Milkshake! (UK), Rai Yoyo (Italy) and TeleTOON+ (Canal+ Poland)**

Toronto, ON – November 30, 2023 – WildBrain has secured a wave of international distribution deals for the beloved animated preschool series, _Brave Bunnies._ The news comes as producers WildBrain, Glowberry, Anima Kitchent and KidsMe launch a brand-new second season of the highly popular series, following last year’s announcement of their global partnership on the brand.

Under the partnership, WildBrain handles global distribution of the series, while Glowberry manages distribution in Ukraine, KidsMe in Italy, and Anima Kitchent in Spain. In consumer products, WildBrain’s leading agency, WildBrain CPLG, handles licensing and merchandising worldwide, outside of Ukraine, where licensing is handled by Glowberry, and Italy, where licensing and merchandising is handled by KidsMe.

![Image 1: Two animated blue bunnies and a teal rhino look right to the viewer and hold up colourful animal toys.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/449abe_bc331138eb8c4cecab947e79cd278c6e~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/449abe_bc331138eb8c4cecab947e79cd278c6e~mv2.png)

The show’s curious and adventurous sibling bunnies, Boo and Bop, continue their global adventure through new distribution partnerships inked with TeleTOON+ (Canal+ Poland), Channel 5’s preschool strand, Milkshake! (UK), and Rai Yoyo (Italy) for both season one and two. Additionally, season one has been newly picked up by CNC Media International (South Korea) and Stan (Australia). Season one is also now available on the WildBrain+ SVOD channel on Comcast in the US. These international deals reflect the global appeal of the brand, adding to the list of platforms in more than 80 countries across LatAm, Canada, the UK, Europe, Nordics, the Middle East, Asia and Australia that have previously picked up the series. YouTube also remains a popular destination for _Brave Bunnies_ fans, where the preschool brand continues to develop a global audience with new uploads each week on the official [Brave Bunnies YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCTtRc8rZrf6753hXFTvl-PQ).

Caroline Tyre, VP Global Sales and Rights Strategy at WildBrain, said: “It’s easy to understand why we continue to see strong demand for _Brave Bunnies_ from broadcasters and streamers worldwide. Through catchy songs, adorable characters and big adventures, the charming series engages kids everywhere, appealing to their sense of joy and imagination. It also fosters values of curiosity, creativity, acceptance and openness, encouraging kids to discover what they might have in common with new friends, while also celebrating what makes them different.”

Olga Cherepanova, Glowberry co-founder and Creative Producer on the series, said: “With _Brave Bunnies_, I wanted to create a series that would encourage children to be curious about the world around them, and to not only respect but celebrate its diversity. It’s rewarding to see children around the world connect so strongly with these important values through the show’s lovable characters and their adventures.”

Aimed at kids aged 2–5, _Brave Bunnies_ (104 x 7’ total) follows Boo and her big brother, Bop, as they travel the world with their Ma and Pa in their Bunny Bus. Season two, which was produced by WildBrain’s Vancouver animation studio and Anima Kitchent’s studio in the Canary Islands, sees the Brave Bunnies continue their road trip adventure around the Bunny World, encountering old friends and making more new ones. Boo and Bop have some big surprises in store for small viewers as they visit their “Best Bunny Friends” at their homes, meeting their families, exploring their unique lifestyles and sharing new adventures.

**For more information, please contact:**

**About WildBrain**

At WildBrain we inspire imaginations through the wonder of storytelling. As a leader in 360° IP management, we are experts in content creation, audience engagement and global licensing, cultivating and growing love for our own and partner brands with kids and families around the world. With approximately 13,000 half-hours of filmed entertainment in our library—one of the world’s most extensive—we are home to such treasured franchises as Peanuts, Teletubbies, Strawberry Shortcake, Yo Gabba Gabba!, Caillou, Inspector Gadget and Degrassi. WildBrain’s mission is to create exceptional entertainment experiences that captivate and delight fans both young and young at heart.

Our studios produce such award-winning series as _The Snoopy Show_; _Snoopy in Space_; _Strawberry Shortcake: Berry in the Big City; Sonic Prime_; _Chip and Potato_; _Teletubbies Let's Go!_ and many more. Enjoyed in more than 150 countries on over 500 platforms, our content is everywhere kids and families view entertainment, including YouTube, where our network has garnered over 1 trillion minutes of watch time. Our television group owns and operates some of Canada’s most-viewed family entertainment channels. WildBrain CPLG, our leading consumer-products and location-based entertainment agency, represents our owned and partner properties in every major territory worldwide.

WildBrain is headquartered in Canada with offices worldwide and trades on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: WILD). Visit us at [wildbrain.com](https://www.wildbrain.com/).

**About Glowberry**

Glowberry is a dynamic Ukrainian creative production company that develops high-quality 360° content for kids and families worldwide, founded in 2009 as a publishing house. Glowberry, now a strategic partner of FILM.UA Group, grew into a production company that works with the best Ukrainian and international professionals to create animated children's content. Company partners are global leaders in animation, broadcasting, film production and licensing. Today, one of the key projects for our team is the _Brave Bunnie_s animated series.

“We believe that creativity, openness to the diversity of the world, and the ability to enjoy life make children's lives exciting, and we are guided by this in our work. We are extremely proud of the team of professional artists and professionals from various fields that we have managed to assemble to work on Glowberry products” – says Olga Cherepanova, Glowberry co-founder and Creative Producer. The projects of the Glowberry professional team are highly acclaimed by international experts and became shortlist finalists of global animation festivals like Cartoon Forum, Animation Production Days, Cartoon 360, Annecy International Animated Film Festival (MIFA), Ottawa International Animation Festival and The Financing Forum for Kids Content.

**About Anima Kitchent**

Anima Kitchent is an animation company with more than 10 years in the animation sector. A team with extensive expertise focusing on creating, producing, distributing, and marketing entertainment brands for children and young audiences. They also offer their services to third-party entities.

Anima Kitchent specializes in creating IPs that can adapt to various platforms including TV, YouTube, apps, web and video games.

Anima Kitchent's most significant project is Cleo&Cuquin - Familia Telerín. This project is accompanied by other productions such as Lea&Pop, Titto Lizzardo, PINY Institute of New York, among others. Anima's content has a strong presence on digital platforms, (Netflix, Cartoonito, Spotify) managing more than 148 YouTube channels with over 43 million subscribers.

**About KidsMe**

KidsMe is specialized in the development, production, content curation and distribution of local and European content dedicated to the Kids&Family target. The Children Content Factory part of De Agostini Editore was born in 2020.

From 2009 to 2020, the Team that is now part of KidsMe has produced and co-produced more than 1,500 hours of content for the target meant for the Group's channels. Today, after a decade of experience, the company has expanded and strengthened its core business focusing on the production and distribution of Live Action and Animation Entertainment content for the Kids&Family target.

Its production focuses on all television genres intended for the target, such as Live Action, Animation, Preschool, Educational, Factual Entertainment and Game Show. KidsMe has produced, co-produced and licensed many products for pay and free-to-air TV channels, such as DeAKids, DeAJunior, Super!, Boing, Rai YoYo, RaiGulp, as well as various contents for OTT platforms like discovery+.

Spikes Asia, celebrating the best of APAC creativity
----------------------------------------------------

2026 Spikes Asia Awards are now open.

### Spikes Asia brings APAC’s creative communications industry together to learn, network and celebrate the power of creativity. At its heart sit the Awards, the region's benchmark for creative excellence, marketing strategy and effectiveness.

![Image 1](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/6clvkT7gS5OrrM4jsfTUOt/a6b684a2ab4a7ee04f64abd1b76376e9/Judging.jpg?w=735)

### Discover the 2026 Spikes Asia Awards

The Spikes Asia Awards are APAC's benchmark of creative excellence. Enter to compete with the region's best work and to showcase your game-changing ideas. Winning a Spike elevates your work to the next level, attracts new clients and talent, and is incontrovertible proof that your work is among APAC's very best.

[Explore the Awards](https://www.spikes.asia/awards)

### Learn from industry leaders' perspectives and insights

![Image 2: In conversation with Hilary Ngan Kee ](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/73Hs2u4Cuxmmkl9wUB6BQE/012e6ada3e26529a66697f7baced0005/SA26_In_conversation_with_Motion_Sickness_1200x675.png?w=576&w=540)

“It was introduced to us as ‘the Impossible Brief’. We knew we’d have to try something new to solve it."
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Motion Sickness' Hilary Ngan Kee shares how creative risk paid off in the indie's award-winning work which put New Zealand on the map as the best place to have herpes.

[Read the interview](https://www.spikes.asia/news/hilary-ngan-kee)

![Image 3: In conversation with Seongphil Hwang, Seungree Kang and Hyoeun Jeon](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/44UBU8cp7ZtOlqpxfX5NtB/cf7b757d6cfd9992f8616762a1ed9066/SA26_In_conversation_with_Cheil_Korea_1096x708__1_.png?w=576&w=540)

Cheil Korea’s Seongphil Hwang, Seungree Kang and Hyoeun Jeon discuss their ground-breaking work for Burger King.

[Read the interview](https://www.spikes.asia/news/seongphil-hwang-seungree-kang-and-hyoeun-jeon)

![Image 4: Daniel Wood, Melissa Hawkett and Claire Stapleton](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/22AjNG4Oovd1dlgiWqUunn/5bd73966e1e57e5a1b02a8adbbdf203f/SA26_In_conversation_with_frog_1096x708.png?w=576&w=540)

“For us, it was great piece of validation, that what was achieved resonated on an even wider level with the most creative and strategic minds in APAC."
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The team at Frog discuss their Spike-winning work ‘The World’s Best Exchange Rate’ and how they made the work a reality.

[Read the interview](https://www.spikes.asia/news/daniel-wood-melissa-hawkett-and-claire-stapleton)

![Image 5: In conversation with  Xu Han and Tingting Zhang](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/2g9LaaOEyDWiI9WXZVXC2I/ac665085f9843162c5401fa4a2ab78c5/SA26_In_conversation_with_TOPic_1096x708_revised__1_.png?w=576&w=540)

“As a small team, we don’t have the resources of big companies, but this award proves the power of creativity and passion."
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Xu Han and Tingting Zhang, Creative Partners at independent agency TOPic discuss the bold idea behind their award-winning work ‘Twin Sister of Olympic’.

[Read the interview](https://www.spikes.asia/news/xu-han-and-tingting-zhang)

### Watch Spikes Asia 2025 highlights

### Winning at Spikes Asia felt like waking up famous — but behind it are years of hard work. Two Grand Prix prove that all barriers are only in our minds. With passion and perseverance, anyone can create world-class work — no matter where they are. Our region’s creative energy is real, and it's only just beginning!

![Image 6: Digital Craft Juror, Yuliya Tushina](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/7s18viovfpUMD4AoBLGzgE/62f33c02d781e8a998237c40fc7da01c/Digital_Craft_Juror__Yuliya_Tushina.webp?w=102&w=129)

### Yuliya Tushina

Chief Creative Excellence Officer

GForce Kazakhstan

### Coming from Pakistan, where pushing for award-winning work is an uphill climb, being shortlisted at Spikes Asia as an independent agency is a huge moment. It proves that creative ambition knows no borders. It shows other indie agencies from emerging markets that their work deserves to be on the biggest stages too — if they just keep pushing.

![Image 7: Shaheryar Ghayas](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/1enpTHECeKQTH2cSeiz8RA/31c55874023777851091942e9d415184/sherry_01__1_.jpg?w=102&w=129)

### Shaheryar Ghayas

Founder & Chief Creative

Madnest

### Spikes Asia has long been a wellspring of inspiration for the creative community. Every experience—from submitting work to receiving recognition and serving as a jury-has left a lasting impact and reinforced my commitment to creative excellence.

![Image 8: Jung A Kim](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/1XyW3GUlDsxk8DRafjzEMb/35bcfb5786b58e121cf9901256175ed8/Jung_A_Kim.webp?w=102&w=129)

### Jung A Kim

Chief Creative Officer

Innocean Korea

### What I like about Spikes is the cultural context it brings; the region has so many cultures and it is amazing to see the variety of work that you get.

![Image 9](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/2wlucY2uDe8kxHwyHIZbh0/feb5704016645d797254b0e7b3917e33/Ali_Rez.jpg?w=102&w=129)

### Ali Rez

Chief Creative Officer

Middle East, North Africa & Pakistan, Impact BBDO

### More insights from top talent

### “Ideas rooted in cultural insights are often the most resonant”

We spoke with the Leo Burnett Taiwan team about their phenomenally successful work, 'Paper Organs’. Learn the story behind the work that won big at both Spikes Asia and Cannes Lions in 2024.

[Read the interview](https://www.spikes.asia/news/hao-tseng-yuan-chuang-and-chin-chin-chiang)

![Image 12: In conversation with Akae Wang and Zita Zou](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/5JsnYgZ1GEAPDYL7GDe38W/4da9d5f736d1706378310d7b9323a485/SA_In_conversation_with_Akae_Wang_and_Zita_Zou_1200x675.png?w=735)

### “That’s the resonance that every creator longs for.”

Banana Balloon’s Head of Creative, Akae Wang, and Creative Director, Zita Zou, discuss their Spike-winning work ‘Answer Me’, and share advice for other Chinese agencies considering entering Spikes Asia.

[Read the interview](https://www.spikes.asia/news/akae-wang-and-zita-zou)

![Image 13: In conversation with Rika Komakine and Tetsuya Honda](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/4omxhTrb3rCUACDuFU57ov/8d19e91381cd84b92caef5cd5ecf674e/SA_In_conversation_with_AjinomotoHonda_Office_1200x675.png?w=735)

### “The entire company is thinking about what we can do to solve our customers' problems and concerns.”

Tetsuya Honda from independent PR agency, Honda Office Tokyo, and Rika Komakine from client, Ajinomoto, discuss the transformative impact the "Frying Pan Challenge" had on Ajinomoto's narrative and its relationship with consumers.

[Read the interview](https://www.spikes.asia/news/rika-komakine-and-tetsuya-honda)

![Image 14: In conversation with Seung-jae Lee ](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/2vdpykJ4BF1dx9zUwL6WK2/acd0aef89d7edcafa307f915deb41e52/SA_In_conversation_with_Seung-jae_Lee_1200x675.png?w=735)

### “The size of the idea is much more important than the size of the company.”

Seung-jae Lee, IDEOT’s Chief Creative Officer and 2025 Direct and Outdoor Juror shares insights into IDEOT’s award-winning work, ‘Park O’Clock’.

[Read the interview](https://www.spikes.asia/news/seung-jae-lee)

![Image 15](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/2H7Z9aVWYUOsGVkRc17Gc3/efa5ea0f31d881d3735a104892ebf445/SA_In_conversation_with_Margaret_Key_1112x640.png?w=735)

### “Creating meaningful, lasting impact is where our true value lies”

The PR Jury President, Margaret Key, shares her views on the sector and gives the inside track on what the Jury will be looking for in 2025.

[Read the interview](https://www.spikes.asia/news/margaret-key)

![Image 16](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/34VlOgXBH7q9Irv896Oe9j/3371b95c28eeeb83f386b30ccd668604/SA_In_conversation_with_Kainaz_Karmakar_1112x640.png?w=735)

### “Craft has to inspire love for the idea”

We talk to Ogilvy India's Kainaz Karmakar about the importance of beautiful craftsmanship and the Design and Industry Craft Spikes.

[Read the interview](https://www.spikes.asia/news/kainaz-karmakar)

![Image 17](https://images.ctfassets.net/5aev5gpxv5kg/6BU5HJAxtNwxB23NhSms0D/75a28e421adf2e26b9275aaf27d6c04e/SA_In_conversation_with_Torsak_Chuenprapar_1200x675.png?w=735)

### “People love stories that are unpredictable”

We talk to WOLF BKK's Torsak Chuenprapar about the thinking behind their entertertaining and award-winning work, _The Air Drummer_.

Times Insider

Before the war, Natalia Yermak was working in Kyiv for a children’s show. Once the invasion began, she started covering the war as a part of a Times team.

![Image 1](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2022/06/01/pageoneplus/01a2_insider-NataliaYermak/merlin_206865960_d2be4769-45a3-42c8-9eae-7b9ac1746254-articleLarge.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&disable=upscale)

Natalia Yermak, left, worked for a children’s show before reporting on the war in Ukraine. She joined a Times team, which included Thomas Gibbons-Neff, right.Credit...Tyler Hicks/The New York Times

June 1, 2022

[Times Insider](https://www.nytimes.com/series/times-insider) explains who we are and what we do and delivers behind-the-scenes insights into how our journalism comes together.

Half an hour before midnight on March 28, the first artillery shell I ever heard screeched above the tiny roof that sheltered my colleagues and me. Our newly formed team had recently arrived in Huliaipole, a small eastern Ukrainian town, to report from the war’s front lines.

A little more than a month earlier, in prewar Kyiv, my job looked a lot different — and it did not involve air-raid warnings or howitzer shells.

It was Wednesday, Feb. 23, the day before the Russian invasion began. I was working as a production coordinator at a company that produced a Ukrainian cartoon series for children called “Brave Bunnies.” The job promised a type of stability that I was ready to embrace after years of on-and-off freelance work in video production.

That day, I was struggling to write an email about an episode in which the brave bunnies meet a koala because nearby my colleagues were discussing the looming Russian presence near our country’s border. “Guys, why worry for no reason?” one of them said. “The news is just feeding communal anxiety. I don’t believe this invasion is going to happen.”

Early the next morning, when the sounds of explosions and air-raid sirens filled the air, that anxiety and disbelief quickly turned into terror.

My reality shattered. The “Brave Bunnies” team decided to put production on hold until the next week, a pause that was destined to stretch out. I packed my bag and boarded an evacuation train headed west, to join my family in Lviv.

![Image 1: Image](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BYmUxMzk3OTQtMjFhYS00MTBlLThkYjEtZTY0MDdkZDM4MzdhXkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_QL75_UX500_CR0,0,500,281_.jpg)

Kids’ entertainment company [WildBrain](https://www.imdb.com/company/co0765605/) has hopped in to save beloved Ukrainian animation “Brave Bunnies,” taking a majority stake in the IP after its production was disrupted by the Russian invasion.

Created by [Olga Cherepanova](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm8898772/), co-founder of Ukrainian kids’ producer [Glowberry](https://www.imdb.com/company/co0782692/), “Brave Bunnies” is a 2D animation for ages 2-5 which tells the story of bunny siblings Boo and Bop. Season 1 sees the duo explore the world around them – bravely seeking out new friends, games and experiences – while fostering values of curiosity, creativity, eagerness, openness and responsibility.

After Russian invaded Ukraine at the beginning of this year, many of Glowberry’s employees were forced to flee Kyiv, leaving the show’s future in doubt. Now WildBrain have partnered with Glowberry and Ibero-American animation studio [Ánima](https://www.imdb.com/company/co0596812/), who co-produced the first season, to ensure “Brave Bunnies” continues to thrive across production, distribution and consumer products.
